prompt:
Write an e-mail to a professor at a British university, inviting him/her to organize a team for international innovation contest to be held at your university.
You should write about 100 words on the ANSWER SHEET.
Do not sign your own name in the email; use “Li Ming” instead. (10 points)
body: I am writing on behalf of the Student Union to invite you to organize a team for the International Innovation Contest, which will be held at our university from May 10 to 15.

The contest aims to bring together young innovators from around the world to share creative ideas. Each team of four to six students will present a project in a field such as clean energy. Given your outstanding achievements in technological innovation, we would be honored if you could lead a team from your university. Accommodation will be provided free of charge.
Please let us know by April 10 whether you can join us. We look forward to your reply.

prompt:
Write an essay of 160-200 words based on the pictures below. In your essay, you should
1) describe the pictures briefly,
2) interpret the implied meaning, and
3) give your comments.
Write your answer on the ANSWER SHEET. (20 points)

【图画】两个学生站在一张“校园讲座”海报前。一个说：“不是我们一个专业的，听了也没有多大用。”另一个说：“去听一下，肯定有好处。”
body: As the pictures show, two students are standing in front of a poster for a campus lecture. One of them is reluctant to attend, saying, “It’s not related to our major, so it won’t be of much use to us.” Her classmate, however, replies, “Let’s go and listen. It’s bound to do us good.”

The pictures reveal two contrasting attitudes toward learning. The first student holds a narrow, utilitarian view, valuing only knowledge directly related to her major. By contrast, her classmate realizes that knowledge from other fields can broaden one’s horizons and spark new ideas. In fact, many breakthroughs come from the intersection of disciplines; for example, advances in biology now depend heavily on computer science. Limiting ourselves to one field may seem efficient in the short term, but it restricts our potential in the long run.

As college students, we should be open-minded learners. Instead of asking whether a lecture will pay off immediately, we should seize every opportunity to explore new areas, attend lectures across disciplines and read widely. Only by doing so can we develop a well-rounded mind and meet the challenges of a rapidly changing world.

type: 电子邮件（介绍 + 邀请）
prompt:
Suppose you are planning a campus food festival. Write an email to the international students in your university to
1) introduce the food festival, and
2) invite them to participate.
You should write about 100 words on the ANSWER SHEET.
Do not use your own name. Use “Li Ming” instead. (10 points)
body: I am writing to tell you about our campus food festival, which will be held in the central square from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. next Saturday. More than 30 stalls will offer a wide variety of dishes, from spicy Sichuan noodles to sweet Cantonese desserts. You can also learn to make dumplings with local students and enjoy live music while you eat.

We warmly invite you to join us. You are also welcome to bring a dish from your home country to share with everyone. If you are interested, please sign up at the Student Union office by Wednesday. We look forward to seeing you there!

prompt:
Write an essay based on the chart below. In your writing, you should
1) interpret the chart, and
2) give your comments.
You should write about 150 words on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points)

【图表】2018—2020 年我国快递业务量变动情况（单位：10 亿件，柱状图）：总体 2018 年 51、2019 年 64、2020 年 83；农村 2018 年 12、2019 年 15、2020 年 30
body: The bar chart illustrates the changes in China’s express delivery volume from 2018 to 2020. The total volume grew steadily from 51 billion parcels to 83 billion, an increase of about 63%. Meanwhile, the rural volume rose even faster, from 12 billion to 30 billion, an increase of 150%. As a result, its share of the total climbed from less than a quarter to over one third.

Several factors contribute to this boom. To begin with, online shopping has become part of daily life, generating a huge demand for parcel delivery. In addition, improved rural roads and logistics networks now allow express services to reach remote villages. Moreover, e-commerce helps farmers sell their produce across the country, which further boosts rural deliveries.

In my view, the rapid growth of express delivery, especially in the countryside, benefits both consumers and the economy. However, billions of parcels also create mountains of packaging waste, so companies should switch to eco-friendly materials and encourage recycling.
